objective: Qualify deterministic codec applicability evidence and, only if justified, a small Lythaus-owned codec-resilient synthetic specialist without modifying SAFE-A.
hypotheses: H1: current-byte codec facts can identify some regimes in which SAFE-A synthetic evidence is materially degraded, but they cannot prove origin.
H2: a small content-derived specialist may rescue some SAFE-A JPEG misses without learning encoder identity.
H3: source-family and encoder-held-out performance will determine whether any rescue is genuine rather than a codec shortcut.
H4: Seedream-4 and Imagen-4 may remain a separate generator-domain problem even if JPEG rescue succeeds.

roles.development: WP007J-R1 real-media JPEG laboratory; score/feature-inspected and never described as independent confirmation.
roles.confirmation: Seven non-FLUX WP007H generator families plus score-blind negative families; no threshold or feature selection after opening.
roles.futureReserve: WP007H SD-3-Medium and Seedream-4.5 remain unopened; FLUX.2 remains sealed.
roles.diagnostic: Previously consumed FLUX.1 public/provider material only after candidate freeze; no tuning.

modelRules.cesE: Deterministic codec/file facts only; cannot emit AI/authorship labels.
modelRules.cesS: Lythaus-owned low-capacity linear specialist only if TRAIN/DEV supports it; no ensemble, vote or average.
modelRules.threshold: Select only from TRAIN/DEV using a specificity-first rule; CONFIRM is single-use.
modelRules.featureSelection: Predeclared content features and TRAIN/DEV stability; no confirmation-informed cherry-picking.

gates.minimumUniqueSafeRescueForSupportCandida: material and repeated across held-out families/encoders; no fixed percentage substituted for evidence
gates.catastrophicShortcutStop: If content features cannot survive removal of encoder/format/quality cues or held-out encoder performance collapses, reject CES-S as a codec specialist.

plannedExperiments: Deterministic CES-E extraction and controlled applicability evaluation.
Lythaus-owned content feature extraction on R1 development and fresh confirmation media.
Linear CES-S development with source-family weighting and shortcut ablations.
Encoder leave-one-out and generator leave-one-out confirmation.
SAFE-A versus CES-S unique rescue and error-correlation analysis.
CPU runtime, reproducibility, rights and evidence-snapshot validation.
prohibitions: No FLUX.2 bytes, pixels, transforms, features, scoring or provider calls.
No production routes, labels, enforcement, database or Safety/Judge changes.
No source media, weights or bulk tensors in Git.
